grammar.title: A plain written predicate: である
grammar.formation: Noun/na-adjective stem + である; negative ではない; past であった. Verbs and i-adjectives keep their plain conjugations.
grammar.explanation: である is a written copula, common in reports and essays. It is not a polite honorific, and it does not make a claim more reliable. In a である-style essay use plain verb endings too: 開催した, not 開催したである. Keep one surrounding written style; a quoted speaker may still say です.
grammar.example: この施設は地域の交流の場である。
grammar.translation: This facility is a place for interaction in the community.

examples.ja: この{施設|しせつ}は{地域|ちいき}の{交流|こうりゅう}の{場|ば}である。
examples.en: This facility is a place for interaction in the community.

examples.ja: {展示|てんじ}は{無料|むりょう}であった。
{講座|こうざ}の{定員|ていいん}は{三十人|さんじゅうにん}ではない。
examples.en: The lecture’s capacity is not thirty people.

grammar.mistake: Do not attach である to a conjugated verb or treat it as business keigo. Plain だ and である overlap in written style, but switching casually throughout a short essay weakens consistency.

grammar.title: Link report clauses with a verb stem
grammar.formation: A verb’s ます-stem can link a written clause: 読みます→読み, 変えます→変え, します→し, 来ます→来（き）. Noun/na-adjective + であり links a copula.
grammar.explanation: The stem can carry a continuing clause in formal writing. The final predicate normally provides the overall tense; context still determines sequence or accompanying actions. Read each clause before joining it. In ordinary conversation the earlier て-form usually sounds more natural. A long chain is harder to follow than two short sentences.
grammar.example: 主催者は会場を変え、前日に連絡した。
grammar.translation: The organisers changed the venue and contacted people the preceding day.

examples.en: The organisers changed the venue and contacted people the preceding day.

examples.ja: {記事|きじ}を{読|よ}み、{要点|ようてん}をまとめた。

examples.ja: {展示|てんじ}は{無料|むりょう}であり、{応募|おうぼ}も{必要|ひつよう}ない。
examples.en: The exhibition is free, and no application is needed either.

grammar.mistake: The final clause still needs a predicate. This is a written-style bridge from familiar stems, not a request to speak to friends in unfinished stem clauses.

grammar.title: Acknowledge a fact, then a remaining contrast
grammar.formation: Verb/i-adjective plain form + ものの; na-adjective + なものの or であるものの; noun + であるものの. Past predicates may also precede ものの.
grammar.explanation: ものの acknowledges the first fact but says a contrasting problem or state remains. It often conveys disappointment: the draft exists, but the title is unsettled. It is somewhat written or considered in tone. In the supported patterns here, the next clause describes the actual result or state rather than issuing a request or inviting a future action.
grammar.example: 下書きはできたものの、題名が決まらない。
grammar.translation: The draft is done, but I can’t settle on a title.

examples.ja: {下書|したが}きはできたものの、{題名|だいめい}が{決|き}まらない。
examples.en: The draft is done, but I can’t settle on a title.

examples.ja: {文|ぶん}は{短|みじか}いものの、{意味|いみ}が{分|わ}かりにくい。

examples.en: The explanation is concise, but there are few concrete examples.

grammar.mistake: A noun cannot take だものの. Do not mechanically replace every けど in friend-chat with ものの.

grammar.title: An outcome contrary to expectation
grammar.formation: Verb/i-adjective plain form + にもかかわらず; noun + にもかかわらず (also であるにもかかわらず); na-adjective + であるにもかかわらず.
grammar.explanation: にもかかわらず presents an outcome that contradicts what the first fact would lead you to expect. It is formal compared with のに and commonly reports an existing or completed situation. Gratitude or criticism can still be conveyed by the context. にかかわらず without も means regardless of and is a different expression, introduced later.
grammar.example: 雨にもかかわらず、大勢の人が来た。
grammar.translation: Many people came despite the rain.

examples.ja: {雨|あめ}にもかかわらず、{大勢|おおぜい}の{人|ひと}が{来|き}た。
examples.en: Many people came despite the rain.

examples.ja: {何度|なんど}も{校正|こうせい}したにもかかわらず、{数字|すうじ}の{誤|あやま}りが{残|のこ}っていた。

examples.ja: {会場|かいじょう}が{狭|せま}いにもかかわらず、{参加|さんか}{者|しゃ}はゆっくり{読|よ}めた。

grammar.mistake: Keep も for despite. Avoid an uncertain future prediction or a request as the second clause in these taught uses.

dialogues.title: Edit the piece, not the friend
dialogues.scene: Misaki and Bao edit Bao’s piece about the reading event. Misaki points to the draft while their own conversation stays casual. They keep the quiet shared reading space as the main idea and move the price list into a small box.

dialogues.title: A short draft and a firm deadline

paragraphs: {電車|でんしゃ}で{読|よ}んでいた{随筆|ずいひつ}を{家|いえ}でも{読|よ}み{返|かえ}した。スマートフォンなら{同|おな}じ{文章|ぶんしょう}をいつでも{開|ひら}ける。それでも、{気|き}に{入|い}った{部分|ぶぶん}は{紙|かみ}に{印刷|いんさつ}した。{画面|がめん}では{短|みじか}く{見|み}えた{一文|いちぶん}が、{紙面|しめん}では{意外|いがい}に{長|なが}かった。{私|わたし}は{句読点|くとうてん}で{止|と}まり、{冒頭|ぼうとう}から{末尾|まつび}までの{流|なが}れを{確|たし}かめた。

スマートフォンは{便利|べんり}であるものの、{通知|つうち}が{来|く}ると{別|べつ}のことを{考|かんが}えてしまう。{紙|かみ}にも{弱点|じゃくてん}はある。{難|むずか}しい{言葉|ことば}をすぐに{調|しら}べられず、{荷物|にもつ}も{増|ふ}える。しかし、{余白|よはく}に{疑問|ぎもん}を{書|か}き、{気|き}になった{文|ぶん}に{線|せん}を{引|ひ}くと、{後|あと}で{自分|じぶん}の{考|かんが}えを{思|おも}い{出|だ}しやすい。{同|おな}じ{文章|ぶんしょう}にもかかわらず、{読|よ}み{方|かた}によって{残|のこ}る{印象|いんしょう}が{違|ちが}うのである。

{友人|ゆうじん}は{画面|がめん}の{方|ほう}が{読|よ}みやすいと{言|い}う。{文字|もじ}を{大|おお}きくできるし、{辞書|じしょ}も{開|ひら}きやすいからだ。{私|わたし}が{紙|かみ}を{好|この}むのは、{誰|だれ}にでも{当|あ}てはまる{結論|けつろん}ではない。{今回|こんかい}は{比喩|ひゆ}や{筆致|ひっち}をゆっくり{味|あじ}わいたかった。その{目的|もくてき}には{紙|かみ}が{合|あ}っていた。{明日|あした}の{通勤|つうきん}では、また{画面|がめん}で{読|よ}むだろう。

{読|よ}み{手|て}が{選|えら}べる{方法|ほうほう}が{多|おお}いことは、{作品|さくひん}に{出会|であ}う{機会|きかい}を{増|ふ}やす。{紙|かみ}か{画面|がめん}かという{賛否|さんぴ}だけでなく、{何|なに}を、どこで、どう{読|よ}みたいのかを{考|かんが}えたい。{手段|しゅだん}を{一|ひと}つに{決|き}めるより、その{日|ひ}の{目的|もくてき}に{合|あ}わせて{選|えら}ぶ。それが{私|わたし}の{今|いま}の{読書|どくしょ}の{形|かたち}である。

glosses.meaning: can open, a text or file here
not being able to look up, connecting negative potential
despite; contrary to the expectation from a fact

options: です and である are mixed in the draft
The two friends always speak in である
The article uses no plain forms
exercises.explain: She points out mixed written predicates, not a problem with their spoken conversation.

exercises.prompt: Where will Bao try placing the table?
options: At the bottom right of the page
At the top left of every photo
On the wall beside the window
exercises.explain: Bao’s last line says 表は右下に置いてみる.

exercises.prompt: What does the table let Bao give more space to in the main text?
options: His experience of reading quietly
A complete list of lecture applicants
An argument that paid lectures should close
exercises.explain: He says the main text can describe 静かに読めたこと.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the noun predicate in consistent である-style writing.
exercises.line: この{施設|しせつ}は{地域|ちいき}の{交流|こうりゅう}の{場|ば}＿＿。
options: である
なある
をある
exercises.explain: A noun predicate takes である; the requested style is explicit.

exercises.context: Form practice: replace 読んで with the ます-stem written connector before the comma.
exercises.line: {記事|きじ}を＿＿、{要点|ようてん}をまとめた。
options: {読|よ}み
{読|よ}む
{読|よ}んだ
exercises.explain: 読み connects a written clause; the final past predicate completes the sentence.

exercises.context: Reply casually to Misaki. You want the rough draft to use plain written style.
exercises.line: {下書|したが}きは、{常体|じょうたい}にそろえるんだよね？
options: うん。「です」が{残|のこ}っているところを{直|なお}すよ。
ううん。{全部|ぜんぶ}「です」にそろえるよ。
うん。{写真|しゃしん}は{二枚|にまい}とも{消|け}すよ。
exercises.explain: The first accepts the requested plain style and states the matching revision; the others contradict it or change the topic.

exercises.meaning: The organisers changed the venue and contacted people the preceding day.
exercises.explain: 変え links the first written clause. The final した supplies past tense.

exercises.prompt: What makes this reading event attractive to the writer?
options: Sharing a quiet time without having to talk
Learning that silent visitors are unwelcome
Buying the most expensive lecture ticket
exercises.explain: The first and last paragraphs develop quiet coexistence, including people who prefer silence.

exercises.prompt: What did the first of the two interviewed visitors say?
options: Seeing others read made them want to open a book
They always read several books at home
The lecture was cancelled because of rain
exercises.explain: The third paragraph identifies the visitor who does not usually read at home.

exercises.prompt: Which activity did the writer’s friend attend?
options: The paid script-reading lecture
Only the free comic display
A proofreading class at city hall
exercises.explain: The second paragraph states 有料の講座 and describes reading the script aloud.

exercises.prompt: When is the finished revision due?
options: Thursday at five
Friday at five
The following Monday morning
exercises.explain: Yamamoto explicitly asks for 推敲 by 木曜日の五時.

exercises.prompt: What is still missing from the main text?
options: Comments from two visitors already interviewed
The name of an organiser they haven’t met
A new opinion from every newsletter reader
exercises.explain: Bao has spoken to two people but has not yet added their comments.

exercises.prompt: When will the newsletter come out?
options: Next Monday
This Thursday
This Friday
exercises.explain: Friday is layout day; publication is 来週の月曜日.

exercises.context: Form practice: use ものの after the noun 草稿 with the written copula.
exercises.line: まだ{草稿|そうこう}＿＿ものの、{内容|ないよう}は{伝|つた}わる。
options: である
だ
な
exercises.explain: A noun takes であるものの, not だものの or なものの.

exercises.context: Form practice: add the taught despite expression, including も.
exercises.line: {雨|あめ}＿＿、{大勢|おおぜい}の{人|ひと}が{来|き}た。
options: にもかかわらず
にかかわらず
だけに
exercises.explain: Despite the rain is the unexpected outcome; regardless of and because of do not express this requested relation.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Yamamoto. You accept the Thursday-five deadline and will proofread before sending.
exercises.line: {推敲|すいこう}は{木曜日|もくようび}の{五時|ごじ}までに{終|お}えてね。
options: はい。{校正|こうせい}もしてから、{木曜日|もくようび}の{五時|ごじ}までにお{送|おく}りします。
はい。{月曜日|げつようび}の{掲載|けいさい}{後|ご}に{送|おく}ります。
はい。{推敲|すいこう}も{校正|こうせい}もしないで{送|おく}ります。
exercises.explain: Only the first accepts both the deadline and the intended proofreading step.

exercises.meaning: Despite proofreading several times, a numerical error remained.
tiles: {校正|こうせい}したにもかかわらず、
{数字|すうじ}の{誤|あやま}りが
exercises.explain: The first completed action leads to an unexpectedly remaining problem, not a future request.

exercises.prompt: Why did the writer print this essay?
options: To savour its figurative expression and writing style slowly
To prove that screens never suit anyone
To avoid reading during the commute
exercises.explain: The third paragraph gives the purpose: 比喩や筆致をゆっくり味わいたかった.

exercises.prompt: Why does the friend prefer the screen?
options: Text size can be enlarged and the dictionary is easy to open
Its margins can only be written on with a pencil
It has no notifications or other distractions
exercises.explain: The third paragraph gives those two concrete benefits.

exercises.prompt: Which conclusion best matches the writer’s view?
options: Choose a reading method to fit the purpose and situation
Always choose paper regardless of the purpose
Stop reading on trains and read only at home
exercises.explain: The final paragraph explicitly favours choosing for that day’s purpose over fixing one method.

grammar: written である and clause stems
unexpected result にもかかわらず
watch.prompt: Optionally read a short essay or report from your own media. Mark its written predicates and one contrast, then retell the main point in ordinary speech.
